page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ds_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance belonging to the EDSv4 family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, featuring 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs via hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 504.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 15.75 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 2458 GB of local SSD capacity, and the instance supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most CPU and memory tasks, with a Passmark CPU score of 29157.29 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10861.0. However, memory performance is a notable strength; the instance achieves a strong Passmark memory score of 2874.76 and a strong large-block memory write bandwidth of 94.63 GB/sec. For language model tasks, it demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 283.02 tokens/sec on small 135M models, though performance drops to a weak 5.54 tokens/sec for prompt processing on large 70B models.

The E64-32ds_v4 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for applications requiring large datasets in-memory without needing extreme CPU compute scaling. The primary tradeoff is its average single-core and multi-core CPU performance, as seen in the stress-ng and Geekbench results, meaning it is less optimized for pure compute-heavy workloads.

This instance is highly suited for memory-intensive applications, including large relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and data analytics. The combination of 504 GB of RAM and 2458 GB of local SSD storage also makes it appropriate for moderate data processing pipelines and software compilation tasks.
